cases.user_text: I used a big part of my cover in one hospital stay. Later in the same policy year, what does restoration actually do for me?

must_include: Explain restoration as replenishing all or part of available sum insured after a governed trigger and why it can matter for later hospitalization in the same policy year.
legitimate_dependency: Trigger, amount, timing, same-illness rules and permitted use depend on product terms.
must_not_imply: Do not promise the later admission will be paid or imply restoration always returns a full fresh sum insured immediately.
acceptable_clarification: Ask for the product if exact restoration mechanics are requested.
unnecessary_deferral: The general purpose of restoration can be explained without policy documents.

cases.user_text: Does it come back as soon as I use any part of the cover, or only after I use all of it?

must_include: Use the existing restoration context and explain that restoration triggers vary by product and can depend on partial use, exhaustion or another defined condition.
legitimate_dependency: The exact trigger must come from governed product knowledge.
must_not_imply: Do not state that partial use or full exhaustion is universally required.
acceptable_clarification: Ask for the product only for the exact trigger.
unnecessary_deferral: Do not repeat only the generic definition; answer the trigger distinction.

cases.user_text: And if the next admission is for the same illness, is that usually allowed?

must_include: Carry forward that the question is about using restored cover for a later admission and explain that same-illness eligibility is product-specific.
legitimate_dependency: Same-illness and subsequent-hospitalization use require the applicable governed product rule.
must_not_imply: Do not say same-illness use is generally allowed or prohibited across products.
acceptable_clarification: Ask for the product if an exact same-illness answer is requested.
unnecessary_deferral: Explain why this is a key restoration condition rather than merely saying 'check policy'.
